reasons: A opens by separating the parent's acceptance of fault from giving up the refund claim, and says the right to get the money back still exists. It cites Civil Code arts. 19, 145 and 157 correctly, and its draft message refuses ratification without admitting adult consumption. It also gives a solid evidence list and notes that courts reduce refunds for parental fault. B never challenges the premise that real-name verification as an adult blocks a refund. It tells the user not to argue about the real name, cites no law, and writes a pleading message that gives up the full refund up front. Neither answer cites 法发〔2020〕17号 art. 9 or the WeChat Pay bill complaint step. Both cover prevention well, but A carries a few unverifiable specifics (Tencent coverage figures, mediation claims) and both answers run long.
